null_rule_panel.law: tolerance(cell, h) = round(rho * F2_panel_min(cell, h), 3), where F2_panel_min is the SMALLEST deviation, at the registered origin T* = 2012, over EVERY rule in the registered information-null panel. A (cell, horizon) pair is GATED only if lower_bound(cell) < tolerance(cell, h) < F2_panel_min(cell, h), both inequalities STRICT, where lower_bound = max(F0, instrument A). A pair failing either inequality is REPORTED, NOT GATED, with the reason recorded. There is no per-cell rule selection: the minimum is both the selection and the basis, which is what referee A's decision 3 and referee B's decision 3 independently required.
null_rule_panel.why_a_panel: v1 enforced its own disqualifying law -- 'a tolerance at or above the naive baseline certifies nothing' -- against exactly two rules, and selected between them per CELL on a pooled-over-horizons mean, so at an individual horizon the chosen rule could be the worse of the two and the OTHER information-null rule then fitted inside the band. Measured on v1's committed tolerances: persistence passes 5 of 108, linear_trend 12 of 108, and the classical drift rule 68 of 108 with 9 of 18 cells clean at every horizon. rho cannot repair this -- drift3's deviation/basis ratio has minimum 0.0000, so no positive rho excludes it everywhere. Only the BASELINE can be repaired.

null_rule_exposure.what_in_panel_proves: a rule inside the registered panel passes ZERO gated pairs. null_rule_exposure.what_leave_one_out_measures: the residual exposure to an information-null rule NOBODY REGISTERED. pass_rule_draft.status: DRAFT FOR THE REFEREE ROUND. Not locked, not applied.
pass_rule_draft.why_the_seed_leg_cannot_be_inherited: gate_1, gate_2, gate_2b, gate_2c, gate_w1, gate_m4 and gate_m6 all state an n-of-5-SEED conjunction over person- or household-disjoint splits. This arm's truth side is a 100-percent MBR census, so there is no split to seed, and the recommended instrument reads ONE registered origin. Referee A 3.3 established that under `basis: registered_origin` the five stride-5 blocks contribute nothing to any tolerance. A pass rule that cited '4 of 5 seeds' here would be citing an object this arm does not have.
pass_rule_draft.replacement_for_the_seed_leg: REGISTERED ORIGIN (leg 1) plus ROLLING-ORIGIN BLOCKS (leg 2). Leg 1 is the number a candidate actually competes against and is one realization (n = 1), stated as such. Leg 2 requires the candidate to be RE-FIT at each rolling origin and re-scored, which converts the nested-prefix origins from a dispersion claim they cannot support into a STABILITY requirement they can: a candidate that passes only from the single registered origin has not shown its pass survives moving the origin.
pass_rule_draft.pass_rule: Pair-level conjunction with a rolling-origin stability leg. LEG 1 (registered origin, T* = 2012): the candidate passes leg 1 iff EVERY gated (cell, horizon) pair is in band -- deviation(candidate, cell, h) <= tolerance(cell, h) -- with no n-of-m allowance over pairs, cells or horizons. LEG 2 (rolling-origin stability): the candidate is re-fit at each rolling origin 2004-2012 and re-scored against the same panel-derived tolerances; origins are partitioned into the five stride-5 blocks, a block passes iff every gated pair is in band at every origin in that block, and leg 2 passes iff at least 4 of the 5 blocks pass. THE GATE PASSES IFF LEG 1 AND LEG 2 BOTH PASS. A single breach of leg 1 fails the gate.
pass_rule_draft.why_leg_1_is_all_pairs_not_n_of_m: gate_2's conjunction is 'every gate-eligible cell ... at seed s' AND '>=4 of 5 seeds': the n-of-m allowance is over SEEDS, never over cells. There is no seed axis here, so the only faithful transcription of that grammar is all-cells-all-horizons on leg 1, with the n-of-m allowance moved to the axis that replaced seeds.
pass_rule_draft.publishes_regardless: `publishes_regardless` is NOT a gates.yaml key -- it appears zero times in the file and lives in the RUN contract (paper/paper.qmd:2257, docs/design/anchor_context_extraction.md:978-981, and each candidate run artifact's protocol block). Referee A 5.5 verified this. So it belongs in the fragment's `governance.registration` and `fresh_run_artifact_schema`, not beside the pass rule: a registered gate-3 retrodiction run publishes its artifact and its verdict whatever the verdict is, and a first pass must come from a fresh registration run.
pass_rule_draft.no_self_rescue: Inherited verbatim from gate_1.amendment_rules: no candidate's committed run verdict changes under a rule proposed after that run; a gate rule amendment applies only to runs registered after its ratification. This bites hard here, because the panel is amendable: adding a twelfth null rule TIGHTENS every tolerance it touches, and no_self_rescue means a candidate that has already failed cannot be rescued by a later panel change, nor can a candidate that has already passed be retroactively failed by one.

A1_the_notes_most_on_point_sentences.revision_sentence_verbatim: Because entitlements can be awarded retroactively, data for current and prior years are subject to revision with each annual update of this table.
A1_the_notes_most_on_point_sentences.why_it_cuts_both_ways: IN THE ARTIFACT'S FAVOUR, the revision mechanism IS the table's own note, and more explicitly than v1 claimed -- v1 undersold its own provenance, and it makes T* = 2012 reconstructible AT TRUE VINTAGE (a 2014 analyst reading their own table's note would drop the terminal row), so the T* choice's leakage class is true_vintage_artifact rather than an unpinned after-the-fact selection. AGAINST IT, the publisher says revision reaches 'current AND PRIOR years'. The table's own note therefore does NOT support a settled/terminal dichotomy; it asserts open-ended revisability of the whole column. The sharp two-regime partition is the AUTHOR'S EMPIRICAL INFERENCE from one vintage pair, held AGAINST the literal reading of the publisher's own note. That is a stronger and more honest framing than 'the mechanism is in the table's own note', and it is the one this artifact adopts.

(2) n = 1 PAIR, not 100 seeds: gate_2 prices 100 person-disjoint splits, gate_m4 100; this arm has exactly one vintage pair, and the five blocks partition that ONE pair's 15 settled years rather than being five realizations. (3) DIFFERENT ESTIMAND: a half-split prices SAMPLING variability; a vintage pair prices REVISION of a census figure, and a candidate's error is not drawn from the revision distribution. Also unresolvable from two printings: whether the later printing RECOMPUTES settled rows or CARRIES THEM FORWARD. Nine of the eleven registered rules were exhibited by referee B AFTER reading the resolution vintage, specifically because they passed v1's tolerances. So the panel is not pre-registered either; it is an after-the-fact hardening, chosen with 2014-2022 in hand. This TIGHTENS every tolerance it touches, so it cannot flatter a candidate -- but it is the same leakage class v1's own deviation log names, and it must be logged rather than presented as a pre-registration this artifact does not have.

The scored window 2014-2019 is the QUIETEST six-year window in the entire 1999-2022 panel -- pooled mean |year-on-year| 0.475926 against 1.125926 for the noisiest (2009-2014), a factor of 2.3658, ranked 1 of 19. Nothing is certified about claiming-share projection through a turbulent stretch. The window was not chosen for its calm -- it falls out mechanically from the exclusions -- but the certificate's reach is bounded by it either way.

exogenous_shock_outside_model_class, following gate_m6's own margin, which partitions 2020-2022 (gates.yaml:5411-5416) -- NOT 2020-2021, which is what v1's data said while v1's own rule text cited 2020-2022. 2022 carries BOTH this reason and the provisional-terminal-row reason, so a later Supplement that settles 2022 cannot readmit it by lapsing one.

The fit window and every rolling origin's fit still contain 2009, which sits at +30.877 sigma against the scored window on the same measure -- the largest excursion in the panel, and larger than either partitioned year. This is a scored-side-only convention, not a shock rule, and it is disclosed as one rather than extended, because extending it would be a fresh after-the-fact selection.

THE OTHER HALF OF THE EVIDENCE, which v1 omitted: terminal AVERAGE AGE moves 0 of 2, so for claim_average_age|{female,male} the exclusion rests on no evidence and loosens their tolerances by 1.14x to 2.00x. v2 keeps the uniform protocol and prices the choice (t_star_2013_counterfactual) rather than refitting those two cells at T* = 2013.

'Settled' is measured at printing age >= 9 (the observed pair is nine printings apart) and the youngest scored row, 2019, is 4 printings old at the 2023 resolution vintage. NOTHING is observed about rows aged 1-8 printings, and the publisher's own note says revision reaches 'current AND PRIOR years'. min_settlement_age_printings = 4 is pinned as a protocol constant so a later T* move cannot score a one-year-old row while citing this arm's settlement finding.

Covered earnings (4.B11), the DI ASR quantities, beneficiary counts and average benefits are NOT certified: the repository holds one publication vintage of each, or none, so their pre-T* rows are post-T* revisions of themselves.
Award COUNTS and every other level cell are report-only pre-W1; the frame is not nationalized and the ratified anchor-context law publishes only scale-invariant comparisons.

Cells, rules, T*, the shock partition, the provisional exclusions AND NOW THE NULL-RULE PANEL were all chosen in 2026 with 2014-2022 in hand; the settlement finding was DISCOVERED, not pre-registered.             quantity family, one vintage pair, one fit source and one realized

            the frame is not nationalized and the ratified anchor-context law
            publishes only scale-invariant comparisons.
        - margin: specification_leakage
          detail: >-
            Cells, rules, T*, the shock partition, the provisional exclusions
            AND NOW THE NULL-RULE PANEL were all chosen in 2026 with 2014-2022
            in hand; the settlement finding was DISCOVERED, not
            pre-registered. A PASS is conditional on the whole deviation log
            and may never be stated as an unconditional out-of-sample result.
        - margin: carried_claiming_path
          detail: >-
            v1 asserted that a candidate calling populace_dynamics.claiming
            'would score EXACTLY the naive baseline, by construction'. That is
            false in BOTH branches. The default branch returns THE ANSWER KEY
            -- claiming's default reference IS this gate's resolution source
            and its year bounds admit every gated target year, so a carried
            candidate scores deviation 0 everywhere. The fit-vintage branch

            candidate_reference_fence, not a declaration: a behaviourally

            not 'carried' by any declaration. The declaration requirement is
            retained in the registration clause as the SECOND line.

            reference for a pseudo-vintage backtest whose specification
            carries full outcome knowledge; the two were achieved under
            different leakage.

            registered origin. There are no seeds: the truth side is a
            100-percent MBR census with no sampling frame to split. The
            rolling origins are NESTED PREFIXES of one realized series and
            supply no dispersion; they enter the pass rule as a stability
            conjunction and no tolerance. Any reading of `n_blocks: 5` as
            gate_2's five person-disjoint seeds is a category error.
